stories.title: BIP-110 Bitcoin fork stalls after just two blocks as gap with main chain widens
stories.summary: A rival Bitcoin branch implementing the contested BIP-110 anti-spam proposal entered mandatory signaling with support from under 3% of miners, according to Cointelegraph. The branch mined only two blocks before stalling out, and CoinDesk reports the attempt began around block 961,632, with the gap versus the main chain continuing to widen since.
stories.whyItMatters: Contested soft-fork attempts test how Bitcoin's decentralized governance handles disputed protocol changes, and even a failed attempt can be a signal of unresolved tension over the network's future rules.
whatToWatch: Whether the branch gains any additional miner support or is effectively abandoned
Any exchange or node-operator guidance on which chain to treat as canonical
Whether BIP-110 proponents attempt a different activation path
questions: What happens to the two blocks already mined on the stalled branch?
Why did miner support come in so far below what backers expected?

stories.title: Canary's XRP ETF pulls in $82 million, but falling prices erase twice that
stories.summary: Canary Capital's XRP exchange-traded fund attracted $82 million in investor inflows, but CryptoSlate reports that a subsequent drop in XRP's price wiped out roughly double that amount in fund value. The result leaves investors who bought in during the inflow period sitting on net losses despite the fund's popularity.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a reminder that strong ETF inflow headlines don't guarantee investor returns when the underlying asset is volatile, especially for newer altcoin-linked products.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows continue or reverse into outflows
XRP's price trajectory in the near term
How rival XRP ETF issuers' funds are performing by comparison
questions: How much of the stated loss is realized versus paper/unrealized?
Are investors who came in early still net positive?

stories.title: Proposed Ethereum upgrade could kill native staking yield, pushing SharpLink's treasury into DeFi
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports a proposed Ethereum protocol upgrade could eliminate a form of "native" staking yield currently available to ETH holders. The change would reportedly pressure corporate treasuries like SharpLink's, which holds roughly $125 million in ETH, to seek yield through higher-risk DeFi strategies instead.
stories.whyItMatters: How Ethereum treats staking yield is central to its economic design, and the outcome could reshape risk-taking by corporate treasuries and institutions that hold large ETH positions.
whatToWatch: Progress of the upgrade proposal through Ethereum's core development process
Whether SharpLink or similar treasuries publicly signal a strategy shift
Any pushback from stakers or institutional holders
questions: What is the specific mechanism being proposed and on what timeline?
How many other corporate ETH treasuries face the same exposure?

stories.title: Grayscale quietly shuts down three altcoin ETFs in under three minutes
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports Grayscale moved to pull three of its altcoin exchange-traded funds in rapid succession, with the process reportedly completed in about 190 seconds. Details on exactly which funds and the wind-down mechanics are limited in the available reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: A major issuer quietly retiring multiple altcoin ETFs suggests thinner demand or conviction for niche crypto products even as broader ETF inflows into bitcoin and other assets remain strong.
whatToWatch: Which three funds are affected and their redemption/wind-down timeline
Whether Grayscale signals plans for other underperforming altcoin products
questions: Which altcoins were behind the closed funds?

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs pull in $853 million in a day, with BlackRock's IBIT taking the bulk
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs saw combined inflows of $853 million, according to CoinDesk, with BlackRock's IBIT fund capturing most of that total. The figure marks a notable single-day pickup in institutional-style demand for exchange-traded bitcoin exposure.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows remain one of the clearest real-time gauges of institutional and mainstream capital moving into bitcoin, and concentrated demand in IBIT underscores BlackRock's dominant share of that market.
whatToWatch: Whether the inflow pace holds over subsequent sessions
How rival issuers' funds compare in flows
Bitcoin's price reaction in the days following
questions: What specifically drove this particular day's inflow surge?

stories.title: Brazil orders up to 24-hour delay on large crypto transfers abroad to curb fraud
stories.summary: Brazil's central bank has ordered crypto exchanges to delay large transfers sent abroad by as much as 24 hours, according to CoinDesk and Cointelegraph, as part of an effort to combat crypto-related fraud. The move gives authorities and platforms more time to flag suspicious outbound transactions before they clear.
stories.whyItMatters: A major emerging-market regulator taking a direct, mandatory stance on crypto transfer delays signals growing global appetite for tighter fraud controls that could influence other jurisdictions.
whatToWatch: Implementation timeline and the transfer-size threshold that triggers the hold
How exchanges operating in Brazil adjust compliance processes
Whether other countries adopt similar transfer-delay rules
questions: What transaction size or risk criteria triggers the hold?
How will this affect legitimate cross-border crypto users and remittances?

stories.title: Bitcoin's 'anti-spam' fork sputters out after mining just two blocks
stories.summary: A contested Bitcoin fork built around the BIP-110 anti-spam proposal ground to a halt after producing only two blocks, according to Decrypt. The attempt appears to have lost momentum almost immediately after launch.
stories.whyItMatters: A failed fork attempt, while low-drama in outcome, still reflects real disagreement within the Bitcoin community over how to handle spam and blockspace policy.
whatToWatch: Whether backers of the proposal try again with revised activation terms
Any commentary from miners or node operators on why support was so thin
questions: Will there be a follow-up proposal, or is BIP-110 effectively dead?

stories.title: Bitwise's Solana ETF draws $267 million, but market losses wipe out all of it

stories.whyItMatters: It reinforces a pattern across new altcoin ETFs this cycle: headline inflow numbers can mask negative real-world returns for the investors funding them.

questions: How much of the loss is realized versus unrealized for current holders?

stories.title: Inactive Bitcoin miner prints 1.65 billion shares to stay afloat with zero revenue
stories.summary: A bitcoin mining company reporting $0 in revenue and 35 idle machines sitting in storage issued 1.65 billion new shares to keep itself operating, according to CryptoSlate. The company's identity and further operational details are limited in the available reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a stark illustration of the distress hitting smaller, undercapitalized miners amid high energy costs and difficulty, and a warning sign of heavy shareholder dilution risk in the sector.
whatToWatch: Whether the company redeploys its idle machines or continues to sit idle
Further dilution, restructuring, or delisting risk
Any disclosed plans to resume mining operations
questions: Which company is this, and why did it go idle in the first place?
Is there a realistic path back to revenue-generating operations?
